To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed an experiment that allows the observation of NOE cross-peaks between protons with degeneracy in 1H and in 15N chemical shift in large proteins and protein complexes.
a projected [1,15N]-HMBC-[1,1H]- NOESY experiment is presented for observation of NOEs between amide pro- tons with degenerate 1N chemical shifts in macromolecular systems.

the projected [1H15N]-HMOQC-[1H, 1H]-NOE experiment provides two spectra corresponding to the two angle projections, which can be combined to give the full spectrum, and the sensitivity of the experiment can be increased by fully exploiting both the proton and nitrogen chemical shift differences, such that short maximum evolution times can be used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for NMR studies of large molecular systems.
the development of new methods for the study of large molecular systems by multidimensional NMR spectroscopy.
the development of novel NMR experiments for the study of large molecular systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new projection experiment can be used to observe NOE interactions between protons with degeneracies of at least three, provided that the degeneracies are not too large, i.e. that the degeneracy is not more than a few times the chemical shift resolution.

the projected [1H-1H]-NOE experiment is the method of choice for observing NOEs in systems with degenerate 1H and/or 15N chemical-shifts, as long as the chemical shifts of the interacting protons are not degenerate.

the projected HMQC-NOE experiment can be used for the observation of NOE signals between degenerate amide protons, and thus can be used as an important complementary tool in the study of the structure of large molecular systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel projection experiment that allows the observation of NOE correlations between amide proton pairs with degenerate 1H and/or 15N chemical shift values, and we demonstrate its application for the study of the linker histone-DNA complex.

we have developed a projection method to separate NOE signals from direct-correlation signals for large proteins with degenerate 1H and/or 15N chemical shift values, which has been demonstrated to work for a 121.5 kDa protein-DNAC.
we have developed a new projection experiment that allows observation of NOE signals between two protons with degenerately overlapping chemical shifts in large proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the projection experiment is a very useful tool for the observation of NOE correlations in large molecular systems with degenerate 1H and/or 15N chemical shift frequencies.

the projected [1H-15N]-HQC-[1H, 1H]-NOESEY experiment provides a simple and effective way of increasing the sensitivity of the 3D [1H- 15N]-HMC-NOESEY spectrum by fully exploiting both the 1H and the 15N frequency difference.

the projected HMQC-NOE experiment is a useful tool for the observation of NOE correlations between degenerate amide protons in large molecular systems and that the projection angle should be chosen according to the particular NOE interaction of interest.
